title: Retry and Backoff Timeline Explorer
description: When the network fails, the Pico retries with exponential backoff: each wait ceiling doubles from a base until it reaches a cap, and there is no wait after the last attempt. The worst case, every attempt timing out and every wait taking its full ceiling, is N x T plus the sum of the N - 1 ceilings. With full jitter each real wait is a random number up to its ceiling, so a jittered run is never longer than the worst case.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Does the wait keep doubling for ever?
Why is there no wait after the last attempt?
Can jitter make the worst case longer?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The wait doubles for ever. (2) The last attempt is followed by a wait. (3) Jitter makes the worst case longer. (4) The waits are the only time a retry costs.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all eight settings. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
